items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What about Al Hanson? Did he give you any specific tips that he learned from Bunk? [INTERVIEWEE] I can't think of any offhand.

ctx.x: Oh, I think louder. I think louder. Lighter than Kid Thomas? Well, yeah, I think Bunk had a more piercing, uh, uh, tone. I mean, it's hard for me to recall now, but he, I know he cut through. I know the band was a very loud band, and there were times when there was a lot of talk, and, uh, a lot of, there were a whole lot of people, there'd be a whole lot of people on the Stuyvesant, a whole lot of talk, and the band would be very loud, and Bunk would just cut through, uh, without, I mean, without any doubt at…

I'm gonna just try to sort of jump around on some ideas. I hope it doesn't confuse you too much. But, you know, I'm getting them from Bill's former tape with it. What about Al Hanson? Did he give you any specific tips that he learned from Bunk?

I can't think of any offhand. Uh, thinking about tips from Bunk, though, uh, there was one discussion I got into with Bill Lofbrower, who apparently had been taking some lessons with Bunk, and he suggested, well, he was suggesting for me to, to move my lower jaw out, and I think that he said that Bunk had suggested this to him, or that he had noticed that Bunk was doing this also, uh, business of throwing the lower jaw forward, which, uh, I think Bunk did that to, uh, to a certain extent, when he played.
